seed_status.title: Arweave Puzzle on Twitter: "The puzzle required 4 steps. My guess is the solver figured out 3 and brute forced one, that's why he is silent.… "

dossiers.four_step_context: ha 225–254, scattered along drawn edges | **Cumulative: on the order of 1,000 candidates, 0 matches, 0 near misses.** A thousand candidates sounds trivially small, and it is — but the number is not the point. What these families exhaust is *every direct, single-transform reading of the measured geometry and the metadata that could be enumerated*: take a measurable property of the image, serialise it, optionally hash it, treat the result as a key. That whole class is dead. What remains is a reading that requires information outside the image, or a bit-level encoding that was never a "whole value" in the first place. ## Where it actually stands This is the weakest-verified entry in its series and the honest label for it is *insight, with no oracle*. Three things are simultaneously true: the target format is certain, the container has been exhaustively characterised, and nobody has any idea what the encoding is. The single most useful structural observation is negative and comes from the sibling. Puzzle #9 was the same shape of puzzle — a private key hidden in an image, an Ethereum prize, the same create-before-modify metadata anomaly — and it *was* solved: its 100 DAI left `0x6f85D220C70abB69a1205B96b566c1eD5d9c3831` on 2020-06-08 06:36:33 UTC in transaction `0x91968c60519866e1a982177ffca22d60520904e53ae6d11814fbc501ad0289bd` (block 10223548, an ERC-20 `transfer` to `0xD8d8bC3bb68eC59a8491Af4257522dFE4F0B9412`). The solver never came forward, and the author's own reading of that silence, four days after asking @_LeFevre_ and @shijint89 "any idea who solved it?", was: **"The puzzle required 4 steps. My guess is the solver figured out 3 and brute forced one, that's why he is silent"** (2020-06-14, 10:18:11 UTC, [1272111084867129344](https://twitter.com/arweavep/status/1272111084867129344)). So the one closely-comparable data point in the entire series is a solve whose method was never published — and when the local research tried to reverse-engineer #9's carrier from its already-known answer as a calibration exercise, that failed too. There is no worked example of this author's steganography anywhere. Three leads, in order: 1. **A systematic bit-level scan of the two continuous channels** (hours). Every candidate so far reads geometry or metadata as a *whole value*, hashed as a block. A genuine LSB sweep of the grayscale channel (256 levels) and the alpha channel (26 distinct observed values) with a tool built for it — `zsteg -a`, `stegoveritas` — across bit orders and bit widths, keeping only 64-hex outputs, has not been run to exhaustion. This is the most literal reading of "format does not matter": a payload in the pixel *values*. Confirmed if an extracted string derives the target address; killed by an exhaustive sweep with no match. 2. **The promised hint, from a channel the archive does not cover** (needs a person). The 55,002-message Telegram archive from November 2021 onward is already searched and contains nothing. What it cannot cover is April 2020 to November 2021, a direct message, or a deleted post — and the original announcement tweet itself is deleted, which shows the author does delete things. 3. **A published method for puzzle #9, if one ever surfaces** (needs new information). That would hand this puzzle its first certified, author-specific extraction scheme, which is precisely what it lacks. It is a standing watch item, not a search. For anyone tempted to price a brute force: there is none. The target is a uniformly random 256-bit integer unless the encoding is found, and 2^256 is not a number you spend money against. ## Sources - Announcement tweet, 2020-04-22 14:06:21 UTC, deleted from Twitter: <https://twitter.com/arweavep/status/1252961944807641090>. **Archived copy**, Internet Archive capture of 2020-05-02 17:38:35 UTC, which carries the full tweet text, the expanded Arweave link, the `data-time` timestamp and the reply thread: <https://web.archive.org/web/20200502173835/https://twitter.com/ArweaveP/status/1252961944807641090>. The Wayback CDX index lists roughly fifty captures of this URL between 2020-05-02 and 2022; the earliest is used here be
